title: Northvale Annual Accounts 2024
text: Road maintenance and repair expenditure in 2024 was 4.2 million pounds. Expenditure in 2023 was 3.4 million pounds. The increase follows the winter storm damage programme approved in January 2024.

title: County Audit Office review of Northvale
text: We checked Northvale's 2024 road repair spending of 4.2 million pounds against ledger entries. The 2023 comparator of 3.4 million pounds agrees with the prior-year audit.

title: Northvale Courier: roads bill rises
text: According to the council's annual accounts, road repair spending reached 4.2 million pounds in 2024, up from 3.4 million. Councillors blamed storm damage.

title: Roads and Rates (blog)
text: Northvale spends about 3.1 million pounds a year on road repair, which is far too little.

title: Community forum thread
text: I heard the council spent 6 million pounds on road repair last year. A scandal!

title: Council press release: storm repair programme
text: Councillors approved an extra 0.8 million pounds for storm damage road repair in January 2024.

title: Transport grant award letter
text: Northvale received a 0.3 million pound government grant towards road repair in 2024.

title: Regional Gazette: council spending
text: Northvale spent 4.5 million pounds on roads in 2024, including a 0.3 million pound government grant, councillors said.

title: Evening Herald: why the roads figures differ
text: The Regional Gazette says Northvale spent 4.5 million pounds on roads in 2024. Residents asked why that is higher than the council's own figure.

title: Northvale pothole dashboard 2024
text: Highways teams repaired 1,350 potholes in 2024, counting both contractor and in-house crews. The target response time for a reported pothole is 10 working days.

title: Highways Partnership annual report 2024
text: Under the main highways contract the partnership repaired 1,200 potholes in 2024. Work by council crews is not included in this total.

title: Operations note: the in-house pothole crew
text: The council's own crew repaired 150 potholes in 2024, outside the main contract. The crew works mainly on residential streets.

title: Northvale Courier: potholes on the up
text: The council's dashboard shows 1,350 potholes repaired in 2024, according to figures seen by the Courier.

title: Community Voice blog: potholes
text: By my count the council fixed only 900 potholes in 2023 and the roads feel worse.

title: Forum: pothole on Mill Lane
text: The council says it repaired potholes in 2024, but the huge pothole on Mill Lane is still there and nobody has come out to look at it.

title: Northvale bus fares policy 2022
text: From 1 April 2022 single bus fares in Northvale are capped at 2.00 pounds until further notice.

title: Northvale bus fares policy 2025
text: From 1 April 2025 the single bus fare cap is 2.50 pounds. This policy replaces the 2022 fares policy.

title: Northvale Courier: bus fare cap rises
text: The council confirmed that the single fare cap will rise to 2.50 pounds from 1 April 2025.

title: Northvale Buses: fares and tickets
text: Single fares on all Northvale town services are capped at 2.50 pounds. Day tickets cost 5.00 pounds.

title: Transport committee minutes, March 2025
text: Members approved raising the single fare cap from 2.00 pounds to 2.50 pounds, effective 1 April 2025.

title: Library service annual report 2024
text: Roof repair at the central library cost 0.4 million pounds in 2024. Visits to Northvale libraries rose by 6 per cent.

title: Waste and recycling: collection changes
text: Residual waste is collected every three weeks from April 2025. Recycling and food waste collections stay weekly.

title: Parks and open spaces plan
text: The council will plant 500 trees in 2024 and repair the bandstand in Riverside Park.

title: Council tax 2025 to 2026
text: Council tax for a Band D home rises by 4.99 per cent in 2025 to 2026, to 2,104 pounds.

title: School places consultation
text: The council proposes 120 extra primary school places in the north of Northvale from 2026.

title: Northvale Courier: new leisure centre
text: The new leisure centre opened in April 2025 and cost 12 million pounds, according to the council.

title: Planning committee: highways depot
text: The road maintenance depot moves to Eastgate in 2026. The old depot site will be sold for housing.

title: Cycling and walking strategy
text: The council plans to spend 1.1 million pounds on cycle lanes in 2024 and 1.3 million pounds in 2025.

title: Winter gritting report 2024
text: Gritters made 62 runs in the winter of 2023 to 2024. The salt budget was 0.2 million pounds.

title: Resident survey 2025 (blog summary)
text: Residents rated roads as their top concern, ahead of bus services and bin collections.
